descriptionChirho: The adverb/conjunction καθώς in its primary comparative function, meaning 'just as, even as, in the same way as,' introducing a clause of comparison, conformity, or manner. By far the dominant usage (182x), covering both manner comparison ('just as he said') and standard conformity ('as it is written'). Multilingual evidence: Spanish 'como, así como,' Hindi 'जैसे, जैसा,' Arabic 'كما,' Korean '같이, 처럼,' Swahili 'kama, kama vile.' This is the standard NT comparative conjunction.

The adverb καθώς used in an indirect question or exclamatory sense, meaning 'how, in what manner,' asking about or marveling at the way something occurs. Attested 1x in the NT. Multilingual evidence reflects the interrogative shift: Spanish 'cómo' (how — with accent, distinguishing it from comparative 'como'), Hindi 'कैसे' (how), Arabic 'كيف' (how), Korean '같이' (overlapping form), Swahili 'jinsi' (manner/how). This rare usage parallels πῶς in function.
